quality_assessment: Chapter is currently a placeholder and needs complete content

issues.description: Chapter needs introduction explaining what glob patterns are and why they're useful
issues.should_add: Explain that -g/--glob provides manual control over file filtering, overriding automatic ignore logic. Mention it complements automatic filtering covered in the dependency chapter.
issues.fix_suggestion: Add introduction section explaining glob patterns as a powerful way to include/exclude files, always overriding other ignore logic

issues.description: Chapter must document the standard glob wildcards supported
issues.should_add: Document wildcards: * (zero or more chars), ? (single char), [ab] (character class), {a,b} (alternatives)
issues.fix_suggestion: Add section showing each wildcard with examples: *.rs, file?.txt, [a-z]*, {foo,bar}.txt

issues.description: Chapter must explain ** for recursive directory matching
issues.should_add: Explain ** matches zero or more directories. Show valid placements: **/foo, foo/**, foo/**/bar
issues.fix_suggestion: Add section on ** with examples and common pitfall: -g foo won't match foo/bar, need -g 'foo/**'

issues.description: Chapter must document ! prefix for exclusion and precedence rules
issues.should_add: Explain ! prefix excludes matching files. Document that later globs take precedence over earlier ones.
issues.fix_suggestion: Add section with examples: -g '*.rs' -g '!test*.rs' excludes test files. Show precedence with example.

issues.description: Chapter must explain that -g can be used multiple times
issues.should_add: Document that multiple -g flags can be combined. Each applies independently. Show examples of combining include/exclude.
issues.fix_suggestion: Add examples showing multiple -g flags working together to refine file selection

issues.description: Chapter must document {a,b} alternative syntax extension
issues.should_add: Document brace expansion: {c,d} matches either c or d. Note: empty alternatives like {,c} not supported. Mention this is ripgrep extension beyond standard .gitignore.
issues.fix_suggestion: Add section with examples: -g '*.{rs,toml}' matches both Rust and TOML files. Note this extends .gitignore syntax.

issues.should_add: Document --iglob for single case-insensitive glob, --glob-case-insensitive to make all -g flags case-insensitive
issues.fix_suggestion: Add section showing --iglob '*.html' matching .HTML files, and --glob-case-insensitive affecting all globs

issues.description: Chapter should explain relationship to .gitignore syntax
issues.should_add: Note that glob rules match .gitignore globs with some extensions (brace expansion)
issues.fix_suggestion: Add note explaining globs use same syntax as .gitignore files, making patterns familiar to git users

issues.description: Chapter needs real-world examples showing common use cases
issues.should_add: Examples: search only Rust files, search all files in a directory tree, exclude test directories, combine multiple patterns
issues.fix_suggestion: Add examples section with: rg -g '*.rs' pattern, rg -g 'src/**' pattern, rg -g '!**/test/**' pattern

issues.description: Chapter should warn about common mistakes
issues.should_add: Common mistake: using -g foo to search directory foo (doesn't match foo/bar). Solution: use -g 'foo/**'
issues.fix_suggestion: Add troubleshooting section highlighting the directory matching pitfall with clear before/after examples

issues.description: Chapter should explain that globs override all other ignore logic
issues.should_add: Emphasize that -g always overrides .gitignore, .ignore, and other automatic filtering
issues.fix_suggestion: Add note that globs provide ultimate control, overriding automatic filtering from dependency chapter

issues.description: Chapter should mention -g as short form of --glob
issues.fix_suggestion: Show both forms in examples, use -g primarily as it's more concise

issues.description: Chapter should document [...] character class syntax
issues.should_add: Document [ab] matches a or b, [!ab] matches any char except a or b. Can use ranges like [a-z].

issues.description: Chapter should explain how to escape special characters
issues.should_add: Document character class notation for escaping: [*] matches literal asterisk
issues.fix_suggestion: Add note on escaping with character classes, mention backslash behavior is platform-dependent
